title.en: Simplifying Export Procedures of Government Commodity
title.orig: Simplifying Export Procedures of Government Commodity

source.name: The LawPhil Project — Arellano Law Foundation

text.en:
To promote the policy enunciated above it is hereby ordered that all existing procedures
involved in the processing of export papers of government commodity agencies shall be conducted in one
place. Such place shall be located at the Bureau of Customs, Port Area, Manila.

To carry out the simplification of export procedures, government commodity agencies shall
provide representatives who shall perform the existing functions of their respective offices, relative to export
procedures. Such representatives shall be deputized by the Heads of their respective offices to perform the
following duties:
a. The Inspectors shall undertake all functions pertaining to the inspection, classification, grading, or
standardization of export products;
b. The Senior Examiners shall grant the proper Government Certificate of Indentification and the Certificate
to Export local products found in order;
c. The Cashiers shall collect the minimum permit fees and/or service fees required by law from the
exportation of Philippine products.

The government commodity agencies which shall appoint and deputize representatives are:
a. Philippine Tobacco Administration
b. Philippine Virginia Tobacco Administration
c. Parks and Wildlife Office
d. Bureau of Fiber Inspection
e. Philippine Coconut Administration
f. Philippine Fisheries Commission
g. Bureau of Animal Industry
h. Food and Drug Administration
i. National Cottage Industries Development Authority

j. Bureau of Plant Industry
k. Bureau of Standards
l. Bureau of Internal Revenue
m. Sugar Quota Administration, other Quota Products Division

The supervision of representatives shall be vested in an Officer-in-Charge who shall be
designated by the National Export Coordinating Center.

All fees collected shall be for the account of the corresponding government agencies which are
lawfully entitled to such fees.

The Auditor General is hereby directed to designate representatives from the General Auditing
Office to audit the various cashiers in the collection and disposition of funds.

Salaries and other expenses of the personnel detailed by various agencies in accordance with the
preceding sections shall continue to be for the account of their respective agencies.

Equipment and supplies necessary for the efficient performance of the representatives shall be
provided for by their respective offices.

This order shall take effect immediately.
Done in the City of Manila, this 17th day of September, in the year of Our Lord, nineteen hundred and
sixty-eight.
(SGD.) FERDINAND E. MARCOS
President of the Philippines
By the President:
(SGD.) RAFAEL M. SALAS
Executive Secretary
